items.title: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Vertically Translated Sine or Cosine Function

sections.normalized_html: What is the minimum value of [MATH: y=\sin x + 2 ?]
sections.readable_text: What is the minimum value of [MATH: y=\sin x + 2 ?]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Method 1

To plot the given curve, we follow these steps:

  • Start with the graph of [MATH: y = \sin x.]

  • Then, shift it by [MATH: 2] units up.

The resulting graph is shown below.

From the graph, we see that the minimum value is [MATH: y = 1.]

Method 2

We know that [MATH: y = \sin{x}] has a minimum value of [MATH: -1.] So, we have

[MATH: -1 \leq \sin x.]

Adding [MATH: 2] to both sides of the above inequality gives

[MATH: − 1 + 2|≤ \sin x + 2; 1|≤ \sin x + 2.]

Therefore, the minimum value of [MATH: \sin{x} + 2] is [MATH: 1.]
